The '''2006–07 FA Premier League''' (known as the '''FA [[Barclays]] Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 15th season of the [[Premier League|FA Premier League]] since its establishment in 1992. The season started on 19 August 2006 and concluded on 13 May 2007. [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] were the two-time defending champions.

On 12 February 2007, the FA Premier League renamed itself simply to the Premier League. The change introduced a new logo, sleeve patches and typeface. The sponsored name remains the Barclays Premier League.

The 2006–07 season was the lowest-scoring season in Premier League history, with only 931 goals (with a 2.45 goals per match ratio, the poorest in the history of Premier League).{{cn|date=March 2024}}

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] won their first Premiership title since [[2002–03 FA Premier League|2003]], following Chelsea's 1–1 draw with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] on 6 May 2007. The result left the defending champions seven points behind United with two games left. It was their ninth title in fifteen seasons.

The three relegation spots were occupied by [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] and [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] who each lasted one season in the league, along with [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] who went down after seven seasons.

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2005–06 Football League Championship|Championship]]. The promoted teams were [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] (playing in the top flight for the first time ever), [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] (playing top flight football for the first time in twelve years) and [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] (returning to the Premier League after a six-year absence). They replaced [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]], [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], who were relegated to the [[2006–07 Football League Championship|Championship]] after their top flight spells of four, two and one year respectively.

|note_res_UC1=Since both [[2007 FA Cup final|finalists]] of the [[2006–07 FA Cup|FA Cup]] (Manchester United and Chelsea) and the [[2006–07 Football League Cup|League Cup]] [[2007 Football League Cup final|winners]] (Chelsea) were qualified for the Champions League, their UEFA Cup spots were given to the 6th- and 7th-placed Premier League teams.
|result5=UC1|result6=UC1|result7=UC1
|col_IC3=#CCCCFF|text_IC3=Qualification for the [[2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup#Third round|Intertoto Cup third round]] 
|note_res_IC3=The highest-placed team who applied for the Intertoto Cup and not in an automatic UEFA Cup spot was awarded with a place in that competition. Blackburn Rovers occupied the Intertoto place, because Portsmouth and Reading did not apply.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/mostpopular.var.1364900.mostviewed.spurs_win_may_harm_rovers_intertoto_chances.php |title=Spurs win may harm Rovers' Intertoto chances |access-date=13 May 2007 |archive-date=20 January 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080120195022/http://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/mostpopular.var.1364900.mostviewed.spurs_win_may_harm_rovers_intertoto_chances.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> A further place in the UEFA Cup was up for grabs via the Premiership Fair Play League. The winner is placed into a draw with the winners of Fair Play leagues in other countries. The representatives from the two countries that come out of the hat first are given a place in the UEFA Cup first qualifying round. Since the winners of the Premiership Fair Play League, Tottenham Hotspur, had already qualified for the UEFA Cup by virtue of their league position, their place in the Fair Play draw was given to Aston Villa. However, the places in the UEFA Cup were awarded to the representatives from Finland and Norway.
|result10=IC3

===Historic goals===
====15,000th goal====
The Premier League expected to have the league's 15,000th goal scored at some point in the period between Christmas and New Year. The target was reached on 30 December when [[Moritz Volz]] scored for Fulham against Chelsea. [[Barclays]], the Premiership's sponsor, donated £15,000 to the Fulham Community Sports Trust in Volz' name.  Additionally, a fan who correctly predicted that Volz would score the historic goal in a contest presented the player with a special award prior to Fulham's game against Watford at [[Craven Cottage]] on 1 January.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.premierleague.com/fapl.rac?command=setSelectedId&nextPage=enNewsLatest&id=1572495&type=com.fapl.website.news.NewsItem&categoryCode=NewsSpecialFeatures |title=VOLZ SCORES 15,000TH PREMIER LEAGUE GOAL |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070123083417/http://www.premierleague.com/fapl.rac?command=setSelectedId&nextPage=enNewsLatest&id=1572495&type=com.fapl.website.news.NewsItem&categoryCode=NewsSpecialFeatures |archive-date=23 January 2007 |publisher=premierleague.com |date=30 December 2006 |access-date=17 May 2007 }}</ref> The honour of scoring the 15,000th goal led to Volz being nicknamed "15,000 Volz".{{citation needed|date=April 2018}}

====Goalkeeper scores====
On 17 March 2007, Tottenham Hotspur [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Paul Robinson (footballer, born 1979)|Paul Robinson]] scored against Watford from an 83-yard free kick, which bounced over his [[England national football team|England]] teammate [[Ben Foster (footballer)|Ben Foster]], who was in goal for the Hornets, leading Spurs to a 3–1 win at [[White Hart Lane]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/6437237.stm |title=Tottenham 3–1 Watford |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 March 2007 |access-date=17 May 2007 |first=Sam |last=Lyon}}</ref> This was the third goal scored by a goalkeeper in Premiership history. The other two were scored by [[Peter Schmeichel]], for Aston Villa against Everton on 21 October 2001,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1606115.stm |title=Schmeichel strike in vain |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 October 2001 |access-date=17 May 2007 }}</ref> and [[Brad Friedel]], for Blackburn Rovers against Charlton Athletic on 21 February 2004.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3496741.stm |title=Charlton 3–2 Blackburn |publisher=BBC Sport |date=21 February 2004 |access-date=17 May 2007 }}</ref> In those two cases, the teams they played for lost. Robinson became the first keeper to score for the winning team in a Premiership match.

==Relegation controversy==
[[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]] escaped relegation on the final day of the season with a 1–0 win over [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], with [[Carlos Tevez]] scoring the winner.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nurse |first1=Howard |title=Man Utd 0-1 West Ham |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/6627803.stm |access-date=3 January 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=13 May 2007}}</ref> [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] were relegated, along with [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton]] and [[Watford F.C.|Watford]]. Tevez was subsequently found to have been ineligible to play, as he was not owned by West Ham, but by a third party. Sheffield United sued to keep their Premier League status and, when that failed, went to an FA arbitration panel seeking up to £30m compensation. The arbitration panel found in favour of Sheffield United.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dollard |first1=Rory |title=Sheffield Utd win ruling against West Ham over Tevez |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/sheffield-utd-win-ruling-against-west-ham-over-tevez-939361.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/sheffield-utd-win-ruling-against-west-ham-over-tevez-939361.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |access-date=3 January 2019 |work=The Independent |date=23 September 2008}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The two clubs subsequently settled out of court for an undisclosed sum,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kelso |first1=Paul |title=West Ham and Sheffield United reach out-of-court settlement over Carlos Tevez affair |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/4981170/West-Ham-and-Sheffield-United-reach-out-of-court-settlement-over-Carlos-Tevez-affair.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/4981170/West-Ham-and-Sheffield-United-reach-out-of-court-settlement-over-Carlos-Tevez-affair.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=3 January 2019 |work=The Telegraph |date=13 March 2009}}{{cbignore}}</ref> while West Ham were fined £5.5 million by the Premier League.
